clue.text: Partly covers superior circuits

parts.note: superior means placed above, over
circuits of a track are laps

explanation.surface: Someone describes a layer that only partly covers a set of upper running tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that partly covers another thing extends across a portion of it, as roof tiles do.

clue.text: Neat ending with soup

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, here one ox
a tail is an end part

explanation.surface: A tidy finish is served alongside a bowl of broth.
explanation.walkthrough: NEAT is an old word for cattle, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a thick soup made from beef tails.

clue.text: Smoke swirling around one coming from the far north

indicators.note: around puts the swirled letters around another piece
swirling smoke moves around, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Smoke curls about someone who has travelled down from the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' rearranges SMOKE as ESKMO, and 'around' places it about I.
explanation.definitionFit: The term, now often replaced by Inuit, describes the Arctic peoples of the far north.

clue.text: Medicine prescribed for workers' group in the county

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: Lincs is the abbreviation of Lincolnshire, an English county
TU is a trade union

explanation.surface: A remedy is prescribed for a labour union in some English shire.
explanation.walkthrough: LINCS is the short form of Lincolnshire, a county in eastern England; TU stands for trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a syrupy cough mixture, a kind of medicine.

clue.text: Matches for seeds

definitions.meaning: to match competitors is to set them against each other
fruit stones, like those in cherries

explanation.surface: Matchsticks are being swapped for seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matches' is a verb here, as in pitting one boxer against another, not sticks for lighting fires.
explanation.definitionFit: To set opponents against each other is to match them; the stones of plums are seeds.

clue.text: Small boys-twins holding article they compiled

indicators.note: holding means one piece clasps the other inside it

parts.note: twin small boys called Ed, a short form of Edward, give two copies of ED
an article is a thing, and IT is a word for a thing

explanation.surface: Two little twin brothers put together a magazine article between them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they' is only a link word; 'compiled' is the definition. ED is a crossword staple for a boy's name, doubled here for the twins.
explanation.definitionFit: To have compiled a book or magazine is to have prepared and arranged it for publication.

clue.text: The problem with horns?

parts.note: a hard choice is said to have two horns, as a bull has, either of which may gore you

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what the trouble with horned animals is.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult choice between two unpleasant options is proverbially described as having horns.

clue.text: Parking inside the ground, uncovers tortoise

indicators.note: inside puts one letter within the word for the ground

parts.note: terrain is ground or land
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: Digging a car park into the land unearths a tortoise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovers' is only a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This freshwater reptile is a kind of turtle, loosely called a tortoise.

clue.text: Bill gets decent coverage but is declining

indicators.note: the word decent gets the bill put inside it

parts.note: a bill is an advertisement, AD

explanation.surface: A piece of legislation is fairly reported but losing support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coverage' is surface dressing; 'gets' signals AD going into DECENT. Bill means a poster, AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in decline is falling into moral or cultural decay.

clue.text: Observe someone steal the money?

definitions.meaning: to observe is to pay attention to something
a thief may literally lift a banknote

explanation.surface: Someone is told to watch carefully as a thief pockets the cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay heed is to attend carefully; read literally, the phrase means pocketing a banknote, cash in paper form.

clue.text: Circle around man of the cloth

indicators.note: around here means the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A ring forms around a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal, but it rearranges the letters of 'Circle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A man of the cloth is a clergyman, someone ordained for religious duties.

clue.text: Shows amusement when I go in for such figures of speech

indicators.note: go in places the single letter inside the word for smiling

parts.note: someone amused smiles

explanation.surface: People grin whenever a speaker uses comparisons.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text had lost the 'I'; 'when' is only a link word, and 'go in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Such figures of speech compare one thing to another using 'like' or 'as'.

clue.text: Fashionable sort of tea to give the lodger

parts.note: fashionable things are said to be in
mate is a South American herbal tea

explanation.surface: A landlady offers her tenant a trendy herbal brew.
explanation.walkthrough: MATE (or yerba mate) is a tea-like drink infused from a South American holly.
explanation.definitionFit: In older usage an occupant who shares a house as a resident, such as a lodger, could be called by this word.

clue.text: Strong grip to be kept on company employee

parts.note: a company is a firm
a hand is a worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: Managers are urged to keep tight control over a member of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the idiom 'keep a firm hand on', meaning to control strictly.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong grip is a metaphor for strict control or discipline over people.

clue.text: Permission to break silence

indicators.note: to break the word silence is to shatter its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks leave to speak up in a quiet room.
explanation.definitionFit: Permission granted by an authority is formal leave, here spelt in the American or verb form.

clue.text: Islamisation achieved. by way of this process?

definitions.text: Islamisation achieved. by way of this process?

indicators.note: achieved suggests the letters are worked into their finished form, an anagram

explanation.surface: A conversion to Islam comes about through absorption into the culture.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the twelve letters of 'Islamisation' rearrange to the process that brings it about.
explanation.definitionFit: Absorption into a dominant culture or religion, such as Islam, is that cultural process.

clue.text: Spaniel that's always jumping up?

definitions.meaning: a breed of spaniel used to flush game

explanation.surface: A dog that cannot stop leaping up is described.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a breed of spaniel; literally it is one that springs or leaps.

clue.text: Sort of shock vote for the rich majority

parts.note: to vote for is to elect

indicators.note: the majority of the word rich is most of its letters, so the last is dropped

explanation.surface: A ballot backing the wealthy few comes as a jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'majority' drops the last letter of 'rich' to leave RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A jolt from a live wire is an electrical kind of shock.

clue.text: Fence is seen to be modified complete reconstruction

parts.note: a paling is a fence of pointed stakes

indicators.note: modified signals that the letters of the two words that follow are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A fence is shown to have been altered into a total rebuild.
explanation.walkthrough: A paling is a fence of pointed stakes; 'to be modified' rearranges the letters of 'is seen'. The surface makes 'Fence' sound like the subject being rebuilt.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means rebirth or regeneration, a total renewal of a thing from scratch.

clue.text: Pointless if their eyes are not open?

definitions.text: Pointless if their eyes are not open?

parts.words: Pointless if their eyes are not open?
parts.note: sewing implements have eyes for thread and are useless with a blind eye or blunt tip

explanation.surface: Something is useless when its eyes stay shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing implements have a point and an eye; without an open eye they cannot be threaded.

clue.text: Baby delivered to a princess

parts.note: a baby is an infant

explanation.surface: A newborn is handed to a royal daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: In Spain and Portugal the king's daughter is given this title.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter of the Spanish or Portuguese king bears this title of princess.

clue.text: The playwright depicting a good emperor

parts.note: PI, short for pious, means good
Nero was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: A dramatist portrays a virtuous Roman ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Wing Pinero was an English playwright of the late Victorian stage; PI for pious is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Arthur Wing Pinero wrote comedies such as The Magistrate.

clue.text: Taking up a tree — try putting in an evergreen shrub

indicators.note: taking up in a down clue lifts the letters so they read from bottom to top
putting in places the word try inside the tree

parts.note: an elm is a tree

explanation.surface: Someone digs up a tree and tries planting a hedge bush instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking up' reverses in a down clue, read bottom to top; it turns the whole container, not just the tree. 'try' looks like a verb but is plain fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This fragrant Mediterranean plant with white flowers is an evergreen bush.

clue.text: Wax where the batsman stands

definitions.meaning: to wax is to grow, as the moon does
in cricket the batsman takes guard in the crease, the marked line in front of the stumps

explanation.surface: Polish and the batter's position at the wicket are put side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wax' looks like polish but means grow; read as two words, the answer is the batsman's position in cricket, inside the line (crease) by the stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax is to grow larger; a cricket batsman stands within the marked line by the stumps.

clue.text: Portrait includes fruit

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Portrait includes fruit (6)': FIG is inside the answer but no clue words supply the surrounding E, F and Y, so the clue appears cut short or misread.

clue.text: Muse on car's first oil change

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word car's
change rearranges the letters of the word oil; that the answer also runs backwards through these words is a coincidence

explanation.surface: Someone reflects on the first oil change of their car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' looks like a verb, ponder, but is one of the nine Greek Muses: the Muse of history.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Muse of history is one of nine goddesses of the arts.

clue.text: Trip over mat, break leg and make such a noise!

indicators.note: to trip over is to be turned head over heels, so the word for a mat is read backwards

parts.note: a mat is a rug

indicators.note: break means the letters of the word leg are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone trips on a rug, breaks a leg and lets out a cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip over' turns RUG to GUR; 'break' rearranges LEG as GLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bubbling throaty sound, like water in a drain or a baby's noise, is that noise.

clue.text: Mournful chap following the map

indicators.note: following puts the word for a man after the plan

parts.note: a map or diagram is a plan
a chap is a gent

explanation.surface: A sad man trails along behind the route map.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a loud, resonant and melancholy sound, hence mournful.

clue.text: Crates which are lost and then found again

indicators.note: lost means the letters of the word crates go astray into a new order

explanation.surface: Boxes go missing and later turn up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like 'discovered' but means cast in metal, so found again means cast again.
explanation.definitionFit: To found metal is to cast it in a mould, so doing it a second time is the answer.

clue.text: Flat out but when jolted one comes to

indicators.note: jolted means the letters are shaken up into a new order

parts.note: one is the article a
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lies unconscious, but a sharp jolt brings them round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when jolted' rearranges A (from 'one') with COMESTO. 'comes to' looks like reviving, the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat out can mean lying unconscious, in a deep stupor.
